steps.name: Two weight matrices
steps.what: W_x turns a 3-number word into 4 numbers; W_h mixes the previous 4-number memory into the next one. The same two matrices are reused at every word.

steps.name: Read word by word
steps.what: Start with a blank memory h, then for each word combine the new word with the old memory and overwrite h. Everything the model knows about earlier words must survive inside these 4 numbers.

values.note: Each row replaces the one above: there is only ever one h.

steps.name: One vector for all

steps.name: The start fades
steps.what: Replace either the first or the last word with ' banana' and measure how much the final h moves. The longer the passage, the less the first word matters, until at 50 words it doesn't change h at all. Attention fixes this: every token looks straight back at every earlier token instead of through one squashed memory.

adam_inside.title: inside optimizer.step()
adam_inside.label: PyTorch AdamW, per weight
adam_inside.src:
# for every weight w with gradient g, at step t
w = w - lr * weight_decay * w                 # weight decay
m = beta1 * m + (1 - beta1) * g               # smoothed gradient   (beta1 = 0.9)
v = beta2 * v + (1 - beta2) * g**2            # smoothed scale      (beta2 = 0.999)
m_hat = m / (1 - beta1**t)                    # bias correction
v_hat = v / (1 - beta2**t)
w = w - lr * m_hat / (sqrt(v_hat) + eps)      # the step

nn.Embedding.text: A lookup table of learned vectors. Call it with integer IDs and it returns the matching rows. Its weight has shape (num_embeddings, embedding_dim).

nn.Linear.text: Computes x @ W.T + b on the last dimension of x. W has shape (out_features, in_features), one row per output.

nn.Dropout.text: In training mode it zeroes each number with probability p and scales the rest by 1 / (1 − p). After model.eval() it does nothing.

nn.Sequential.text: Runs its modules in order, passing each output to the next.

nn.Parameter.text: Marks a tensor as a weight of the module, so it shows up in model.parameters() and gets trained.

nn.Module.text: The base class for every layer and model. Calling a module runs its forward method.

Dataset.text: Anything with __len__ and __getitem__. A DataLoader uses those two methods to fetch items.

DataLoader.text: Pulls items from a Dataset, optionally in a random order, and stacks them into batches.

nn.functional.cross_entropy.text: Applies log-softmax over the last dimension of input, picks the log-probability of each target index, and returns the negative mean.

torch.softmax.text: Exponentiates and normalizes along dim so the values there are positive and sum to 1.

torch.triu.text: Keeps the upper triangle of a matrix and zeroes the rest. With diagonal=1 it keeps only what is strictly above the diagonal: the future.

tiktoken.get_encoding.text: Loads GPT-2’s byte-pair tokenizer, with a vocabulary of 50,257 tokens.

torch.optim.AdamW.text: Adam with decoupled weight decay. Each step moves every weight by its own scaled amount and shrinks it slightly toward 0.

history.summary: Map created: training flow, evaluation and sampling, and four study lines (Tokenizer, Data loader, RNN, Attention)

summary.text: Turns one long text into training pairs: it encodes the text with the tokenizer, slides a window of max_length tokens along it every stride tokens, and pairs each window with the same window shifted one token on as its target.

does.text: Builds input_ids and target_ids in its constructor, so indexing returns one (input, target) pair of tensors.

summary.text: Wraps GPTDatasetV1 in a PyTorch DataLoader with the GPT-2 tokenizer, so training reads shuffled batches of input and target windows.

gotchas.text: It always passes drop_last=True to the DataLoader, whatever its drop_last argument says, so an incomplete last batch is dropped even when the caller asks to keep it.

summary.text: The sizes every model class reads: vocabulary, context length, embedding width, heads, layers, dropout and the query-key-value bias, at GPT-2 small's 124M-parameter settings with a shorter context.
The whole model: token and position embeddings, n_layers TransformerBlocks in sequence, a final LayerNorm and a linear output head that scores every vocabulary token at every position.

does.text: Adds the token embedding of each id to the embedding of its position, then applies dropout before the blocks.
Returns logits of shape (batch, tokens, vocab_size); the output head has no bias.

summary.text: One transformer block: LayerNorm, multi-head attention and dropout added back to a shortcut, then LayerNorm, feed-forward and dropout added back to a second shortcut; the shape of its input and output is the same.

Causal multi-head self-attention: it projects every token to queries, keys and values, splits them into n_heads heads, masks out later tokens, and mixes the values by softmaxed, scaled scores before an output projection joins the heads.
Normalizes each token's vector to mean 0 and variance 1 over its emb_dim numbers, then applies a learned scale and shift.
The position-wise feed-forward network: a linear layer to four times emb_dim, GELU, and a linear layer back, applied to each token on its own.
The activation inside FeedForward, in the tanh approximation GPT-2 used.

The training loop: for every batch of every epoch it clears the gradients, computes the batch loss, backpropagates and steps the optimizer, evaluating every eval_freq steps and printing a sample after each epoch.
The loss of one batch: the model's logits against the target ids, flattened across the batch and positions, under cross-entropy.
The average batch loss over the first num_batches batches of a loader, or every batch when none is given.
Measures the training and validation loss over eval_iter batches each with dropout off and no gradients, then puts the model back in training mode.
Prints 50 tokens the model generates from a starting text, with dropout off.

gotchas.text: It calls text_to_token_ids, generate_text_simple and token_ids_to_text, which no notebook in the folder defines.

summary.text: What one batch does inside train_model_simple: the loss runs the model forward through every block, then backward and the optimizer change every weight.

trigger.text: Every batch of every epoch, in train_model_simple's inner loop.

steps.label: optimizer.zero_grad() clears the last batch's gradients
token plus position embeddings, then each of the 12 blocks in turn
norm1, then attention: each token looks at the ones before it
context vectors, added back onto the shortcut
norm2, then the feed-forward network on each token
the same shape out as in, into the next block
loss.backward(), then optimizer.step() moves every weight
